description: External Agent direct API (/api/v1): Bearer-PAT-only caller resolution with Project grants, idempotent launch/follow-up/stop, strict PublicExecutionRead served from a durable checkpointed projection, and resumable per-Session public events.

tasks.title: PAT Project grant model and grant-aware issuance (server + CLI)
tasks.description: Add the persisted direct-API Project grant to credentials per D2/D10: a DirectApiProjectGrantKind column on CredentialRow plus a CredentialProjectGrants child table (unique per pair), with invariants explicit ⇒ non-empty set, operator_all ⇒ empty set, absent kind ⇒ direct API denied (pre-existing PAT behavior). Extend POST /api/auth/tokens with projectIds[]/allProjects validated in order (mutual exclusion → allProjects requires operator scope → every ID resolves as a private Project) and persisted in one transaction, and add `--project` (repeatable) / `--all-projects` to `mo auth token create` with client-side mirrors of the same rules.
acceptanceCriteria: An additive EF Core migration adds DirectApiProjectGrantKind and CredentialProjectGrants (unique index on CredentialId+ProjectId) without semantically altering existing tables; existing nullable ProjectId integration binding is untouched

Grant issuance is atomic: a failed binding (both grant forms, --all-projects without operator scope, or an unknown/non-private Project) returns 403 and persists neither Credential nor grant rows, verified by asserting zero rows after failure

Issuance with repeated --project persists an explicit grant with exactly the listed set; --scope operator --all-projects persists an operator_all grant with an empty set; operator_all is persisted explicitly and never inferred from an operator scope at resolution time
A PAT created without grant options remains fully usable on existing control-plane surfaces (existing auth spec tests stay green)

The full token is shown exactly once by the CLI and only its hash is stored; CLI option parsing rejects --project together with --all-projects and --all-projects without operator scope before any request
Spec-test scenarios for the PAT Project grant model and Grant-aware PAT issuance requirements pass, including explicit-grant scoping, absent-grant denial, and atomic unknown-Project failure
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Auth (Credential grant model, issuance validation, migration), packages/cli grant options, unit + spec tests
tasks.notes: Grant is a property of one credential and dies with revocation; the child table gives per-pair uniqueness and issuance-time FK validation against Projects (ProjectRefResolver).

tasks.title: Bearer-only /api/v1 sub-surface: ExternalAgentCaller resolution and authorization ordering
tasks.description: Create the ExternalAgent module and /api/v1 route group per D1/D3: AuthResolutionMiddleware gains a BearerOnlySurface rule so /api/v1 skips the mohist_session cookie fallback, and a new ExternalAgentCallerResolver endpoint filter loads the Credential's scopes and persisted Project grant into a per-request ExternalAgentCaller (callerKeyId, principalId, scopes, projectGrant, allowedProjectIds). Implement the shared procedural authorization pipeline (caller → route scope → Project grant without resolving the Project → resource membership → header/JSON validation) so every route mapped into the group enforces the security contract by construction.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to any /api/v1 path carrying only the mohist_session cookie and no Bearer PAT returns 401 unauthenticated with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and resolves no ExternalAgentCaller; trusted Agent Connection identities are never consulted on this surface
Missing, malformed, expired, and revoked Bearer tokens are indistinguishable: uniform 401 unauthenticated with the same Bearer challenge
An out-of-grant projectId returns 403 forbidden without any Project-resolution lookup (403-before-404 verified against a nonexistent Project), and grant checks read only the persisted grant
Write endpoints require operator scope and read endpoints accept readonly or operator: a readonly caller on a write route gets 403 before any resource lookup, idempotency, or admission work

401/403 paths create zero durable side effects: no request-mapping read or write, no rejection tombstone, no canonical record, no outbox item, no public event, no Runner/provider contact — asserted against every relevant store, with only the AuthAuditEvent written
Pipeline unit/integration tests pin the ordering caller → scope → grant → membership → validation as observable behavior
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/ExternalAgent (module scaffold, route group, Identity resolver + ordering pipeline), AuthResolutionMiddleware BearerOnlySurface rule, tests
tasks.notes: Reuse the existing middleware rather than a MapWhen branch or per-route re-resolution: one authentication path makes 'cookie cannot substitute' a property of the surface. Resource-membership (404) conventions are exercised end-to-end by the route tasks T-005..T-008.

tasks.title: PublicExecutionRead strict allowlist DTO and five-state aggregate evaluator
tasks.description: Implement D8 as a pure, dependency-free component: a dedicated 22-property PublicExecutionRead DTO serialized by its own writer (every key always present, nulls only where the canonical fact does not exist, observedAt always, output null or {"text"}, error null or {code,message}), plus PublicStatusProjector.Evaluate implementing the fixed precedence exactly as specified. This is the privacy boundary every route and the projection will serialize — never AgentJobLaunchRead/AgentSessionRead/SessionInputRead/TurnResultRead/SessionOperationRead.
acceptanceCriteria: Exhaustive serializer tests assert the response key set is exactly the 22 allowlisted properties — no extra key, no missing key — across accepted/queued/running/terminal/unknown fact combinations

Precedence unit tests cover each spec scenario: fenced terminal wins over late observations; durable rejection is terminal with outcome=rejected and null live IDs; unresolved acceptance/dispatch/binding/stop/outcome facts project unknown (admission=blocked when a Session exists); outcome_pending is running with admission=blocked; retryable dispatch block stays queued+blocked; running beats queued beats accepted
Input/Turn evaluation is anchored to the requested record: a terminal target stays terminal inside an active Session and sessionActivity is reported as context

No-internal-leak tests: no code path emits runtimeSessionId, Runner IDs, runtime names, binding epochs/fences, operation/attempt IDs, dispatch details, prompt or input text, memory, workspace, paths, or raw provider/Runner errors
Direct-API error envelope {"error":{"code","message"}} with safe codes/messages is defined alongside the DTO and covered by tests
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/ExternalAgent (PublicExecutionRead DTO + dedicated serializer, PublicStatusProjector.Evaluate), unit tests
tasks.notes: Allowlist DTO, not a deny-list over product read DTOs — deny-lists rot as product DTOs grow fields. unknown/outcome_pending must expose no code path that authorizes replay.

tasks.title: Durable checkpointed public projection: projector, journal, stream states, snapshots
tasks.spec: specs/external-agent-execution-read/spec.md#A durable checkpointed public projection serves all reads
tasks.description: Implement D7 plus the projector-side event-resume facts: four new tables (PublicExecutionSnapshots, PublicSessionEvents, PublicStreamStates, PublicProjectionCheckpoints) with an additive migration, and a single projector hosted background service that consumes AgentJobEventRow/AgentSessionEventRow plus canonical row snapshots (EventPushQueue wakes it; a durable poll loop is the source of truth) and commits affected snapshots + journal entries + stream allocation + checkpoint in one EF transaction. Snapshots are T-003's PublicExecutionRead; the journal uses exactly the eight-type public vocabulary with per-Session strictly increasing sequences and generation one created on first commit.
acceptanceCriteria: One projection transaction commits snapshot + journal + sequence + checkpoint together: a crash before commit leaves no partial state and a crash after commit resumes past the checkpoint without emitting a second sequence for the same normalized source transition (kill-between-transactions test)

Journal vocabulary is exactly input.accepted, input.rejected, turn.queued, turn.running, turn.outcome_pending, turn.terminal, session.unknown, session.context_reset; execution events carry an execution field that is exactly PublicExecutionRead; session.context_reset carries only the smaller session payload with no jobId/inputId/turnId/output/error/prompt
Sequences are strictly increasing per Session across generations and never reused or renumbered; stream generation is stable across restart, crash recovery, and outbox replay
Terminal snapshots store the internal terminal fence/revision and stale, delayed, or replayed outbox facts cannot un-terminal a target or replace recorded outcome/output/error
Job-anchored snapshot rows exist from the Job prepare fact onward (addressable before Session acceptance with null live IDs) and are updated in place after acceptance
A route-facing required-watermark check distinguishes lag from unknown and drives the 503 projection_lag decision; unknown is emitted only from consumed, inconclusive durable facts
First-deploy backfill replays existing durable history from checkpoint zero in bounded, throttled batches without starving request-path writes
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/ExternalAgent/Projection + Infrastructure/Data/ExternalAgent stores + migration + hosted projector service, spec/unit tests
tasks.notes: Projector must not source from SignalR/the event bus — the bus only wakes it. Keep transactions small and batched per wake-up (SQLite single-writer). Rebuild/generation-swap is future work; generation plumbing lands now so cursors can bind to it.

tasks.title: Launch and follow-up routes with durable idempotency mappings
tasks.spec: specs/external-agent-write-idempotency/spec.md#The first request durably maps key and fingerprint to its canonical outcome
tasks.description: Implement the two write commands per D4/D5 plus the follow-up derivation rule: POST .../agents/{agentId}/launch and POST .../agent-sessions/{sessionId}/inputs behind the T-002 pipeline, with required Idempotency-Key validation (400 idempotency_key_required/_invalid), strict single JSON parse rejecting unknown/duplicate properties (400 invalid_request, v1 body only required non-empty text), a versioned SHA-256 fingerprint over contract version + command kind + canonical scope IDs + canonical body JSON (text preserved byte-exactly), and the DirectAgentRequestMappings table driven by the reserve (pre-minted canonical IDs) → drive (IAgentLauncher.LaunchIdempotentAsync / Session follow-up path with pre-minted Input/Turn IDs) → finalize protocol. Launch drives never pass the caller's raw key into the launcher: derive the D4 scope-qualified coordinator key (SHA-256 over direct-launch-v1 || projectId || agentId || callerKey, -delimited tag, no fingerprint or callerKeyId input) and pass the byte-exact prompt with ExactPromptFingerprint=true. Responses are 200 PublicExecutionRead served from the projection with the watermark check.
acceptanceCriteria: A lost launch or follow-up response retried with the same key and identical payload returns the same canonical Job/Session/Input/Turn (or Input/Turn) identities and creates no second Job, Session, Input, Turn, queue entry, or outbox item (identity-idempotent replay test)

A key reused with a different normalized fingerprint — including text differing only by whitespace or case — returns a stable 409 idempotency_key_reused with no new effect; semantically identical bodies differing only in JSON key order or insignificant whitespace match the same fingerprint
Only the fingerprint is persisted; the raw body is never stored and the fingerprint never appears in any response or public event

A definitive canonical admission rejection is finalized as the mapping outcome and replayed as 200 status=terminal outcome=rejected with null live Input/Turn IDs forever, including after capacity recovery; it is never turned into a newly accepted execution
A pending mapping (crash between reserve and finalize) re-drives the identity-idempotent pipeline or returns the current observation / 503 projection_lag — never a second execution

Same Idempotency-Key on a different Agent in the same Project is a fresh execution: the reserve succeeds, the drive lands on a distinct scope-qualified coordinator grain (derived key differs), and no 409, no cross-Agent replay, and no stuck pending mapping results

A product-route launch and a direct launch using the identical key string in the same Project do not interfere in either direction: the direct drive uses the derived coordinator key (never the raw caller key), so neither surface replays, conflicts with, or 409s the other
LaunchIdempotencyConflictException raised below the direct layer is surfaced as a 500 internal invariant violation, never translated into a caller-facing 409 idempotency_key_reused

The follow-up resolves the Session first and derives Project and Agent from the canonical Session record; no body or query value can select a different Agent, and unknown properties, attachment references, or caller-selected execution options fail 400 invalid_request before admission
Command routes return 200 once the durable keyed outcome is known and the body's status field, not the HTTP code, is authoritative; an ahead watermark yields 503 projection_lag with no stale state
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/ExternalAgent (Routes + Idempotency: mapping table + migration, fingerprint, reserve/drive/finalize, launch + inputs routes), spec tests
tasks.notes: Direct fingerprint is its own versioned gate (the launcher trims the prompt, the direct contract must not) while launch still funnels through the same coordinator engine. The coordinator key derivation is deterministic over exactly the launch scope (projectId, agentId, caller key) so it mirrors the mapping scope: same scope+key replays the same grain, different scope lands on a different grain, and the -delimited tag cannot appear in any caller-suppliable key, so direct and product key spaces cannot collide. Recommendation for the open question: extend AgentSessionFollowupReservation to adopt pre-minted Input/Turn IDs, mirroring the launch coordinator.

tasks.title: Keyed stop route: caller-bound mapping to one canonical fenced stop operation
tasks.spec: specs/external-agent-write-idempotency/spec.md#A keyed stop maps to one canonical fenced stop operation
tasks.description: Implement POST .../agent-turns/{turnId}/stop per D6 on top of the T-005 mapping infrastructure: the stop mapping is caller-bound (turnId scope plus callerKeyId/projectId/sessionId columns), the reserve transaction freezes the stop target (Turn revision, context generation, binding-or-explicit-null, deadline) and the Server-generated internal operationId as internal-only columns, and the route drives the existing canonical lifecycle — already-terminal Turn is a durable no-op with no Runner call, queued Turn ends locally via StopQueuedTurnAsync recorded cancelled without Runtime contact, running Turn goes through ClaimTurnStopAsync → dispatched → CompleteTurnStopAsync with the frozen facts. A different key while the fenced outcome is unknown returns 409 stop_outcome_unknown; the same key recovers a lost response.
acceptanceCriteria: The first keyed stop durably freezes the target before any Runner effect; a later binding, context, or owner change cannot redirect the stop to replacement work, and a matching retry returns the current Turn observation without re-reading the binding or recomputing the deadline
An already-terminal Turn produces a durable no-op observation with no Runner call; a queued Turn ends locally recorded cancelled without contacting Runtime

While a stop outcome is unknown, a different Idempotency-Key on the same Turn returns 409 stop_outcome_unknown with no new stop operation or external effect, and the caller reads the Turn; the same key resolves the same mapping and never creates a replacement effect
A different caller reusing another caller's key against the same Turn does not resolve the first caller's mapping — it is evaluated as a fresh keyed stop subject to the unresolved-stop conflict rule

Completion-vs-stop races resolve through the terminal fence (MarkTurnTerminal): exactly one terminal fact wins, at most one terminal public event, and a late observation cannot replace the winner's outcome, output, error, or sequence

Frozen facts (revision, context generation, binding, deadline, internal operationId) never appear in any response or public event; the route accepts no caller-named Runner, Runtime Session, dispatch attempt, or operation ID
Session admission stays blocked while a stop is unresolved and no automatic replay occurs; recovery is the existing stop-recovery reminder bounded by the frozen deadline
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/ExternalAgent (stop route + caller-bound frozen-target mapping), spec tests
tasks.notes: Composes the current claim/complete contract and adopts #562's fence semantics when it lands — the direct mapping layer stays independent of that internal evolution. The key is the caller-visible identity; internal operation IDs are never caller-facing.

tasks.title: Per-Session public events route with opaque tamper-evident cursors
tasks.spec: specs/external-agent-event-resume/spec.md#One persisted public event route per Session
tasks.description: Implement GET .../agent-sessions/{sessionId}/events per D9, served exclusively from the persisted PublicSessionEvents journal: optional opaque `after` cursor and `limit` (default/max 100), pages carrying sessionId, ascending events, nextCursor, and highWaterSequence, with strictly-after resume. Cursors are base64url(canonicalJson({v, keyId, projectId, sessionId, generation, after}) || hmac) signed from the secret-store keyring with key-id rotation support; decode failure, tampering, cross-Project/Session, or old-generation binding returns 400 cursor_invalid. Closed-stream tombstones and the retention floor return 410 cursor_expired with safe bounds.
acceptanceCriteria: A cursorless first page returns the earliest retained events of the current generation ascending with a nextCursor after the last event; resume with `after` returns only strictly greater sequences; limit is clamped to default 100 and max 100
nextCursor equals the last event's cursor on a non-empty page and sits at highWaterSequence on an empty page; each event carries exactly sequence, cursor, type, and occurredAt
A tampered, malformed, cross-Project, cross-Session, or superseded-generation cursor returns 400 cursor_invalid with no fallback, no translation, and no event read

A valid current-generation cursor resuming before the earliestSequence floor returns 410 cursor_expired including the safe earliestSequence and latestSequence bounds; the Server never silently restarts at the stream start or head

Control-plane Session deletion closes the stream with a minimal tombstone: a valid current-generation cursor gets 410 cursor_expired with earliestSequence=null and the last safe latestSequence, a cursorless read gets 404 session_not_found, and a purged tombstone yields 400 cursor_invalid
The route reads only the persisted projection — an in-flight Runner or in-memory notification arriving before the projection transaction commits mints no cursor, sequence, or payload for this route
HMAC key rotation is additive: old key ids verify for the cursor-retention window without mass-invalidating live cursors
tasks.notes: v1 retains all events while the Session lives; transcript compaction must not touch the journal. Cursor content contains only IDs the caller already knows but stays documented as opaque data.

tasks.title: Job, Input, and Turn read routes and the pinned seven-route surface
tasks.spec: specs/external-agent-execution-read/spec.md#Job read is the status recovery path
tasks.description: Implement the three resource reads — GET .../agent-jobs/{jobId}, GET .../agent-inputs/{inputId}, GET .../agent-turns/{turnId} — served only from the projection with one strict PublicExecutionRead each, behind the full T-002 pipeline. The Job read is the status recovery path (prepared-before-acceptance, durable rejection, post-acceptance progression, lost-launch retry anchoring). With this task all seven v1 routes exist, so the route surface is pinned by a route-enumeration test.
acceptanceCriteria: A prepared Job before Session acceptance returns 200 with jobId, status=accepted, jobStatus=preparing, and null sessionId/inputId/turnId; a durably rejected Job returns 200 status=terminal outcome=rejected with safe error/reasonCode and null live IDs; after acceptance the same read exposes the public Session/Input/Turn references and later status/output/error as projected
An absent or cross-Project Job/Input/Turn returns 404 job_not_found / input_not_found / turn_not_found only after the grant and scope pass, and is never confused with the public state unknown

A lost launch response is recovered by repeating the launch with the same key (same Job anchor or 503 projection_lag) followed by the Job read, with no replacement Job created (end-to-end recovery test)

Reads are anchored to the requested record: a terminal Input/Turn stays terminal inside an active Session with sessionActivity as context; a readonly PAT with a valid grant can observe all three reads
A route-enumeration test asserts the /api/v1 surface contains exactly the seven specified routes and no Runner, Runtime, workspace, transcript, operation, or internal-event route
An ahead required watermark on any read returns 503 projection_lag and never serves stale projection state as current
tasks.notes: The enumeration test lands here because this task completes the seven-route surface; the API adds no second execution lifecycle, queue, or event bus.

tasks.title: Flip docs and design status to implemented and document caller resume rules
tasks.spec: specs/external-agent-event-resume/spec.md#Documented dedup and ordering rules for resuming callers
tasks.description: Per D11, after routes, issuance, and the projection are demonstrably wired, flip docs/agent-api.md from wip-not-implemented to implemented, document the grant options in docs/auth.md, update the Status sections of design/agent-api.md and design/auth.md, refresh `mo auth token create` CLI help, and document the caller-side resume rules (store nextCursor only after durably processing a page, dedup by (sessionId, sequence), apply in ascending order, resume from the last contiguous cursor or reread the target Input/Turn on a gap).
acceptanceCriteria: docs/agent-api.md status flips from wip-not-implemented to implemented with no remaining 'do not build against this' warning, and its route/idiom documentation matches the shipped seven-route surface
docs/auth.md documents --project/--all-projects grant options, mutual exclusion, the operator-scope requirement for --all-projects, and that ungranted PATs cannot call the direct API
design/agent-api.md and design/auth.md Status sections move from wip/target to implemented

The documented caller resume rules state: a retried GET may repeat a page, concurrent pages may arrive out of order, dedup by (sessionId, sequence), apply ascending, never infer a missing transition from a later sequence, and store nextCursor only after durable processing
CLI help text for mo auth token create covers the new grant options
tasks.output: docs/agent-api.md, docs/auth.md, design/agent-api.md, design/auth.md status sections, CLI help
tasks.notes: Docs are the shipping signal, not the starting artifact — they flip last, after the surface they describe exists and its tests pass.
